Congressman Tim Burchett, the House's most outspoken voice on UFO transparency, joins Tucker Carlson to discuss new underwater sightings and what he calls the non-human technology the government is hiding. Burchett argues from his seat on the oversight side: agencies spend, classify, and refuse to answer, and he names the stonewalling as the scandal.

Carlson shares the premise and lets the congressman catalogue the reports, including objects seen entering the ocean. Burchett's authority is procedural rather than technical; he knows where the money and the files sit. The claims themselves remain unverified, and the episode is preserved as his case. Listeners get the disclosure movement's congressional face explaining, in plain Tennessee terms, why he believes the cover-up is real and what he intends to do about it.

Tucker Carlson lays out what he calls the government's mass censorship campaign. He walks through how officials leaned on tech firms to mute speech. Posts on health, votes, and war all faced removal.

The title promises everything a viewer needs to know on the subject. Carlson cites files and suits that showed state requests. He argues the system hid behind private firms to dodge the First Amendment. The episode builds one long case, step by step. It suits listeners who want the full map of a machine they may have felt but never seen.
